questions.question: What exactness condition on g1,g2 enables the potential G and the paper's later energy conservation law?

options.C: g1+g2=0, so G is identically zero
options.D: g1g2=1, so G is the product u1u2

questions.rationale: The symmetric cross-partial condition makes the nonlinear vector field a gradient and is explicitly cited as needed for the conservation law.

questions.question: What spectral assumptions are imposed on each convolution kernel βi?

options.A: Its Fourier transform is nonnegative and bounded above by Ci(1+ξ²)^(−ri/2)
options.B: Its Fourier transform is strictly negative and grows as |ξ|^ri
options.C: The kernel itself is pointwise nonnegative and compactly supported
options.D: Its Fourier transform vanishes outside |ξ|<Ci and is otherwise constant

questions.rationale: The main kernel hypothesis is the two-sided spectral bound, with nonnegative transform and polynomial decay.
questions.evidence_quote: 0 ≤ bβi(ξ) ≤ Ci(1 + ξ2)−ri/2 for all ξ

questions.question: For the exponential kernel β(x)=½e−|x|, what local coupled system results after applying 1−D²x?

options.C: The fourth-order Boussinesq system with both a and b nonzero
options.D: A KdV system first order in time with quadratic dispersion

questions.rationale: The exponential is the Green's function of 1−D²x, and applying that operator yields the coupled improved Boussinesq equations.
questions.evidence_quote: Then, applying the operator 1 − D2x to both sides of equations (1.1)-(1.2) yields the coupled improved Boussinesq equations

questions.question: What is the regularity threshold and kernel-decay requirement in the local well-posedness theorem?

options.A: s>1/2 and r1,r2≥2, with data in Hs
options.B: s≥0 and r1,r2>3, with data only in L1
options.C: s>3/2 and r1,r2=1, with analytic data
options.D: s=1/2 and arbitrary ri, with compact support

questions.rationale: Theorem 2.4 states local well-posedness for Sobolev exponent above one-half and both decay exponents at least two.

questions.question: What blow-up alternative characterizes the maximal existence time for a local solution?

options.A: Finite Tmax requires the Sobolev norms of U and Ut to become unbounded as t approaches Tmax
options.B: Finite Tmax occurs exactly when the conserved energy becomes negative
options.C: Finite Tmax requires the kernel Fourier transform to acquire a zero
options.D: Finite Tmax occurs when either component reaches a spatial maximum

questions.rationale: The maximal-time criterion is divergence of the Hs norms of the solution vector or its time derivative.

questions.question: Which scalar functional and concavity condition underpin the paper's finite-time blow-up proof?
questions.rationale: The proof applies the concavity lemma to this augmented squared-P norm, choosing b and t0 to make the functional positive and increasing.

questions.question: What are the key sufficient hypotheses in Theorem 4.2 for finite-time blow-up?

options.A: A growth inequality ui fi≤2(1+2ν)F and negative initial energy E(0)<0
options.B: Positive initial energy and globally Lipschitz nonlinearities
options.C: A nonnegative potential G and kernels with ri>3
options.D: Zero initial velocity and a strictly positive kernel transform

questions.rationale: The theorem assumes the stated potential-growth bound and negative initial energy to force the concavity functional to blow up.

questions.question: For sufficiently smooth kernels, what lower-bound condition on G supports the global existence theorem?

options.A: G(a,b)≥−k(a²+b²) for all a,b, with r1,r2>3
options.C: G(a,b)=0 only at the origin, with r1,r2<1
options.D: G(a,b)≥k(a²+b²), with no restriction on ri

questions.rationale: Theorem 5.1 uses the quadratic lower bound together with decay exponents above three and applies Gronwall to control higher Sobolev norms.
questions.evidence_quote: If there is some k > 0 so that G(a, b) ≥ −k(a2 + b2) for all a, b ∈ R

questions.question: How does the paper define the 'mildly singular' kernel class used for its second global-existence theorem?

options.A: β(x)=γ(|x|), with γ∈C², γ(0)>0, γ′(0)<0 and γ′′∈L1∩L∞
options.B: β is smooth at zero with γ′(0)=0 and γ′′ not integrable
options.C: β is a compactly supported step function with a jump in β itself
options.D: β has a Fourier transform supported at finitely many isolated frequencies

questions.rationale: The class permits a first-derivative jump at zero and assumes the stated smoothness and bounds on γ.

questions.question: What nonlinear growth condition is imposed in Theorem 5.2 for global existence with mildly singular kernels?

options.B: Each gi must be globally bounded by a constant independent of G
options.C: The sum g1+g2 must vanish for every pair (a,b)
options.D: Each gi must grow at least exponentially in |a|+|b|

questions.rationale: The theorem controls Lqi norms of the nonlinearities using the potential plus a quadratic allowance, enabling the pointwise energy estimate.
